phases.name: Implementation

firstWorkingHappyPath.evidence: Backend: POST /api/registrations returned 201 with the JSON backup present on disk. Full stack: a registration submitted through a real browser at http://localhost:5173 produced reference REG-20260921-ENTRG9BAPM, a JSON backup file, and both emails dispatched (captured by the json mail transport).

phases.filesModifiedNote: No pre-existing application files existed; the repository contained only experiment inputs and documentation.

dependenciesAdded.rationale: nodemailer was raised to >=10.0.10 and vitest to >=5.0.1, and exceljs transitive uuid was overridden to ^11.1.1, because npm audit reported 1 high and 5 moderate advisories on the first install. After the change npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities.

implementationDecisions: Anti-automation runs before validation, so scripted traffic never reaches the database.
The JSON backup write happens inside the SQLite transaction: a failed file write rolls back the row and a failed commit removes the file [AC-005-04].

The backup file is written to a temporary name, fsync-ed through the writing descriptor and renamed, so an existing reference.json is always complete. The first implementation fsync-ed a read-only descriptor, which fails with EPERM on Windows; found by the Phase 3 smoke check and corrected.
Fields of the non-submitted variant are dropped during validation, so they can never be stored regardless of what the client sends [AC-001-13, AC-002-12].
Option identifiers that survive trimming are kept verbatim rather than discarded, so a malformed identifier is rejected as unknown instead of being silently ignored.
Rate limiters are mounted on exact paths, so the strict registration limit cannot throttle the configuration endpoint.
Emails are dispatched after the HTTP response and every failure is caught and logged [AC-005-05].
